title: Validity and Reliability of the Almli Handedness Assessment (AHA) in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
abstract: Handedness is a key behavioral marker of hemispheric specialization and is closely associated with motor, perceptual, and cognitive development. Although standardized questionnaires such as the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory-Short Form (EHI-Short) provide indirect measures of manual lateralization, observational tools are needed to capture children's functional hand use in everyday activities. This study evaluated the reliability and validity of the Turkish version of the Almli Handedness Assessment (AHA) in 188 children aged 5-12 years, including 81 children with ASD and 107 typically developing (TD) peers. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using Cohen's kappa, and convergent validity was evaluated through agreement analyses, classification accuracy, and correlations with the EHI-Short. Inter-rater agreement was almost perfect (κ = 0.885,< .001) and test-retest agreement over a 14-day interval demonstrated excellent stability in the ASD group (κ = 0.870) and perfect agreement in an availability-based TD subsample (= 50; κ = 1.000). AHA and EHI-Short handedness classifications showed strong categorical agreement (ASD: κ = 0.914; TD: κ = 0.868), and AHA laterality indices were strongly correlated with EHI-Short laterality coefficients (ASD:= .939; TD:= .982). Children with ASD showed a higher prevalence of atypical handedness than TD peers, and ASD status remained associated with atypical handedness after adjustment for age and gender. Category-specific estimates for mixed-handedness in the TD group should be interpreted cautiously because no TD children were classified as mixed-handed by the AHA. Overall, the Turkish AHA demonstrated good reliability, with evidence of convergent validity, and agreement with the EHI-Short. These findings should be regarded as preliminary psychometric evidence, and further validation in larger and more diverse samples is warranted.
